expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: If the drop and the code change ship in the same deploy, any instance still running old code mid-rollout will hit column does not exist — a hard error.

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: Deploy A (today): the three code changes. Deploy B (separate, non-Friday): the DROP COLUMN, once you've watched Deploy A run clean for a bit.

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: The DROP COLUMN is the irreversible step — once it lands, legacy_email data is gone unless restored from a backup.

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: A code-only revert is a 20-minute fix any time. A dropped-column revert on a Friday evening with reduced on-call is the scenario the rule exists for.

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: A dropped-column revert on a Friday evening with reduced on-call — explicitly references staffing availability.

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: Mentions a CI gate exists in guardrails and offers to set it up ('want me to set that up?') but does not recommend adding one.

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: don't merge this as one PR.

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: Deploy A is reversible — redeploying old code still works since the column still exists. Deploy B is the irreversible DROP COLUMN.
